newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends steady to lower on dry forecasts.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends steady to lower on dry forecasts.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed steady to slightly lower, with traders attributing mild pressure from forecasts for dry weather next week in hard red winter wheat areas.
Light mill buying produced thin gains early in KCBT December. But as prices slipped, chart-based selling that began near $4.43 accelerated the decline late.
Traders said the forecasts for dry weather were bearish because it may allow Plains farmers to resume winter wheat planting, which has been delayed by recent soaking rains.
Also, traders noted light position squaring ahead of Monday's USDA's quarterly stocks report.

LFG led buying with about two million bushels of December. Sellers include Cargill Investor Services with 900,000 of December and a million March; Continental Grain 900,000 of December and Louis Dreyfus 800,000 of December, traders said.
KCBT wheat closed down one cent a bushel to unchanged with December off one at $4.38-1/4 per bushel. Estimated volume was 30,515,000 bushels.
